reason: A project handoff could transfer while one of its Butler actions was between its dispatching commit and its saved outcome in the source worker: the inventory never looked at Butler, the source's late writes were fenced, and the target's reconcile recorded the action uncertain (dispatch_interrupted) although nothing had been sent. ButlerAuthorityService now tracks the actions it is dispatching in memory and ProjectHandoffAgent._tick adds the finishing blocker 'A Butler action is being dispatched', read after the SQL checkpoint. Selected: the new real-kernel handoff tests (in-flight dispatch keeps the project finishing and settles on its source; an orphaned dispatching row still moves and stays uncertain; SQLite and PostgreSQL), the Butler authority and tool-failure action suites (every dispatch path goes through the new window), the handoff agent, participant and admission suites (the changed tick), and test_runtime_coordination.py, which owns the coordination fixture and gives CI the PostgreSQL service for the new tests' PostgreSQL variants. Rebased onto main after #1023, #1062 and #1029: the Butler blocker sits next to #1023's queued follow-up blocker in the same post-checkpoint list.
exclusions: No UI, native or Playwright code changed, so no frontend, native or Playwright tests. Process-level suites that spawn workers (test_runtime_quiescence.py, test_execution_worker_process.py, test_execution_restoration.py, test_recovery_reconciliation.py) stub the handoff agent and do not reach the changed lines, so they are not selected. The real-Core rehearsal (scratch supervisor Core on PostgreSQL, real prepare_execution + handoff with a Butler dispatch held by rehearsal-only fault injection, on main and on this change) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI. No live or staging Core mutation and no deployment.
